title: The Retention Supplement on a Resort Lodging Early Departure
content:
A retention supplement is added on the room rate retained from a Resort Lodging stay, because a night given back in the busiest weeks is the hardest to let again. How much is added turns on how the nights the reservation covers sit against the unit type's published rate windows. The holiday window runs from the 19th of December 2026 to the 2nd of January 2027 inclusive, and the peak window from the 3rd of January 2027 to the 14th of March 2027 inclusive.

Where every night the reservation covers falls inside the unit type's published holiday window, the holiday retention share of the room rate retained, being 25 percent of it, is added to it.

Where every night the reservation covers falls inside its published peak window, the peak retention share of that amount, being 10 percent of it, is added to it.

In every other case nothing is added.

| How the nights the reservation covers sit against the published windows | Added on the room rate retained |
| --- | --- |
| Every night inside the holiday window | 25 percent of it |
| Every night inside the peak window | 10 percent of it |
| Any other case | nothing |

### Three hypothetical reservations, where the room rate retained is 1200.00 USD

A reservation covering the nights of the 21st to the 27th of December 2026 has every night inside the holiday window, so 300.00 USD is added, being 25 percent of 1200.00 USD.

A reservation covering the nights of the 5th to the 11th of February 2027 has every night inside the peak window, so 120.00 USD is added, being 10 percent of 1200.00 USD.

A reservation covering the nights of the 30th of December 2026 to the 5th of January 2027 has some nights inside the holiday window and some inside the peak window, so every night falls inside neither window alone, and nothing is added. It is the nights the reservation covers that are read, not only the nights retained.
